decisions.decision: NEVER merge v0.0.2, any other milestone, PR #16, or any other PR until the operator explicitly says so
decisions.rationale: The merge is gated behind ADDITIONAL code reviews and security reviews, which are themselves gated behind proving everything the milestone claims. So 'all the evidence is in' is NOT an argument for merging -- it is the argument for STARTING the reviews. That is the inference an agent gets wrong, because from inside the proving step the work looks finished and a green board reads as permission.

decisions.decision: Temporary pushes to main ARE approved as the instrument, with backup-before and restore-after; pushing any branch and opening/closing any PR are also approved
decisions.rationale: The counterpart to the merge prohibition, so a merge is never needed as a measurement device.

decisions.decision: Item 3 runs as THREE hops, not two
decisions.rationale: A push event runs the workflow at the PUSHED TIP. The restore lands on fe25a3f, which predates the gate, so it runs the UNGATED workflow. The skip direction is still provable without merging by rewinding to a tip that DOES carry the gate -- hop 2 -- and the final restore is suppressed by disabling the workflow.

decisions.decision: PR #16 is CLOSED before the open push and REOPENED after the restore
decisions.rationale: Its base is main and its head is the branch being pushed there, so with it open GitHub auto-closes it AS MERGED and sets mergedAt -- a de-facto merge reached by an action nobody would call merging. Precedent: PR #12 was closed first for this reason during the Phase 13 window.

context_notes: The window is the only stateful operation in this milestone -- everything before it was append-only commits, safe to abandon halfway. It is paused here deliberately, fully prepared, so it starts with a full context budget. THE WINDOW IS OPEN WHENEVER origin/main != fe25a3f; the plan's RECOVERY section detects and closes it from any of seven death points, and it is on the remote. Two lessons from this session bear directly on the window. FIRST: five independent passes -- planner, two plan-check rounds, code review, verifier -- all missed that a push event runs the workflow at the PUSHED TIP, because every one of them read the workflow in the working tree and none asked which commit's copy executes. A blind spot shared by every pass is a different failure class from a gate nobody checked, and re-running the same shape of review would never have found it. SECOND: the window plan's own pre-registered observation for phase 9 was IMPOSSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION -- publish-verify is a per-leg self round-trip that ENFORCES reader == producer, so the linux-producer line it asked for on the Windows leg is the exact condition the assertion rejects. The stale expectation was in the SOURCE ROW, inherited unexamined. Executed as written it would have spent the window and left the row open, or closed it falsely by loose-matching a neighbouring line. Also carry the measured false-zero shapes, each of which reads as confident absence: a literal spanning a line wrap (fired three times, once on the sweep correcting it); rg -U with \s+ cannot bridge a wrap whose continuation carries a '#' (use [\s#]+); a SHAPE-anchored regex failing because a file records verdicts as headings not table rows; git grep needing -e for a dash-leading pattern; and rg -rn being parsed as --replace n, which returns plausible prose with every match overwritten. Always check the exit code (1 = genuine no-match, 2 = the command FAILED) and run a positive control on the same path.
